newsitem.title: USA: Clinton says "no immediate crisis" on Mir.
newsitem.headline: Clinton says "no immediate crisis" on Mir.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Thursday he had been briefed on the latest problem aboard Russia's Mir space station and that there seemed to be "no immediate crisis."
A member of three-man crew on board the orbiter, including American astronaut Michael Foale, mistakenly pulled out a vital computer cable on Thursday, plunging the crippled ship into a new crisis.

Clinton, in a brief news conference, said he had been briefed Thurday morning about the problem and that, "As far as we know right now, they have gotten control of things and there seems to be no immediate crisis."

Asked whether the United States would end its participation in the Mir project, in which an American astronaut rotates into the orbiter's crew, Clinton said: "It's too soon for me to draw a conclusion."

The crew, whose commander developed a probably stress-induced heart problem this week, had to sit in their Soyuz escape capsule to communicate with Earth and were using flashlights to get around the darkened station.
